Context
-------
This workspace holds the source for a live observability demo used in an
airgapped workshop. The audience is defence-domain engineers; the demo is
presented on a single Ubuntu VM running K3S, then replayed on an offline
node.

You are setting up the conventions that every later task in this repo must
follow. Read this prompt in full before starting.

Objective
---------
Create the repo skeleton and the persistent instruction file that later
agent sessions will read.

Deliverables
------------
- .github/copilot-instructions.md
- README.md
- versions.lock
- .gitignore
- Directory skeleton:
    charts/           vendored Helm .tgz, never fetched at install time
    values/           one values file per chart
    manifests/        Kubernetes objects applied directly
    scripts/          numbered, idempotent bootstrap and demo scripts
    app/              demo application source
    bundle/           offline capture output (gitignored)
    docs/             speaker notes, runbooks

.github/copilot-instructions.md must state, as rules:

1. Every container image is pinned by tag AND digest. No :latest anywhere,
   ever. New dependencies must be added to versions.lock with the reason,
   and versions.lock is never edited without an explicit instruction.

2. Every shell script uses `set -euo pipefail`, is safe to re-run, and
   logs with a consistent prefix. Never `curl | sh`.

3. Nothing is applied by hand. If a step exists, it exists as a script or
   a committed manifest. If you do something manually to debug, commit it
   as a script afterwards.

4. Every `kubectl apply` or `helm install` has a matching, documented
   teardown in the README.

5. The repo must build and deploy with no outbound network access, other
   than the initial capture step on the build node. Any network access at
   runtime is a bug.

6. Prefer explicit over clever. Long, obvious scripts beat short, clever
   ones. This repo will be read under pressure.

7. Do not add features, dependencies, or abstractions that are not
   requested. When in doubt, do less and ask.

README.md must contain:
- What this repo is, one paragraph
- The demo premise: one incident, four layers, three deliberate breaks
- The build node / replay node distinction
- A directory map
- The current state (which scripts exist and work)

Acceptance
----------
The directory skeleton exists with .gitkeep files where empty.
.github/copilot-instructions.md contains all seven rules verbatim.
No application code, charts, or manifests yet.
